title: Given the root of a binary tree, return its node values grouped by level, from top to bottom and left to right within each level. Explain the Tree Breadth First Search pattern.
shortTitle: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal (BFS Level by Level)

s1_definition.oneliner: Use a queue, snapshot the level size, drain exactly that many nodes while enqueuing their children, producing one list per level.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Tree BFS pattern** – visit nodes level by level using a FIFO queue.
- **Level-size snapshot** – at the start of each level, record `queue.size()` to know how many nodes belong to this level.
- **Drain and enqueue** – dequeue exactly that many nodes, collect their values, and enqueue their non-null children.
- **Result** – a list of lists, each inner list holding one level's values left to right.
- **Complexity** – O(n) time, O(w) space where w is the maximum width of the tree.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India prints its approval hierarchy rank by rank. The branch manager is at the top, department heads on the next rank, then clerks. To list staff rank by rank, you start with the manager in a queue, process them, add their direct reports to the back of the queue, and keep processing one full rank at a time.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Binary tree level order traversal is the foundation of the Tree Breadth First Search pattern. It uses a FIFO queue plus the level-size snapshot: at the start of each level, capture the current queue size, drain exactly that many nodes while enqueuing their children, and collect each level's values into its own list. This cleanly separates levels without depth markers.

The level-size snapshot is the reusable core that every Tree BFS variant builds on. Zigzag traversal flips direction per level. Right-side view takes the last node per level. Minimum depth stops at the first leaf. Maximum depth counts levels. Connect siblings wires next pointers. All use the same queue loop.

At the National Bank of India, this rendered the approval hierarchy rank by rank. The branch head sat at the root, department heads on level 1, and officers on level 2. Processing the tree with a queue and grouping by the level-size snapshot produced each rank's approvers for the audit report.

The senior trade-off is BFS versus DFS space. BFS uses space proportional to the widest level (O(n/2) for balanced trees), while DFS uses space proportional to height (O(log n) balanced, O(n) degenerate). For wide trees, DFS may be lighter. Understanding this trade-off and articulating that the level-size snapshot is the universal BFS building block is what signals real understanding.

Remember one sentence: Snapshot queue.size() at each level's start, drain that many nodes while enqueuing children, and every Tree BFS variant is just a modification of how each dequeued value is used.

---

keyPoints: Level-size snapshot: capture queue.size() before draining to isolate each level.
Drain exactly levelSize nodes, enqueuing their children for the next level.
Result is a list of lists, each inner list holding one level's values left to right.
The snapshot is the reusable core for all Tree BFS variants (zigzag, right view, min depth).
Time O(n), space O(w) where w is the maximum width of the tree.
BFS space is O(width); DFS space is O(height); choose based on tree shape.
